title: L10 · Upper Extremity
subtitle: Shoulder girdle, scapula, humerus, radius and ulna, wrist and hand

lines.text: Let's walk down the arm.
The **clavicle** and **scapula** form the shoulder girdle.
The **humerus** is the arm.
The **radius** and **ulna** are the forearm.
Then the carpals, metacarpals and phalanges.
The clavicle is a small S-shaped bone.
It runs from the sternum to the acromion.
Its medial end meets the manubrium at the **sternoclavicular joint**, or **SC**.
Its lateral end meets the acromion at the **acromioclavicular joint**, or **AC**.
The **medial border** is closest to the spine. It's also called the vertebral border.
The **lateral border** faces the armpit. It's the axillary border.
They meet at the bottom at the **inferior angle**.
The **superior angle** is at the top of the medial border.
The **glenoid fossa** is a shallow socket on the lateral scapula.
It meets the head of the humerus. That's the glenohumeral joint, the shoulder.
The **supraglenoid** tubercle is above it.
The **infraglenoid** tubercle is below it.
The **spine** of the scapula is a ridge on the back. You can't see it from the front.
Its root sits about level with **T4**.
It ends laterally at the **acromion**, the high point of the shoulder.
The **coracoid** process is a finger pointing forward, lower than the acromion.
The scapular notch is just medial to the coracoid.
The **supraspinous** fossa is above the spine.
The **infraspinous** fossa is below it. It's almost the whole back.
The **subscapular** fossa is on the front, against the ribs.
The **head** of the humerus points medially.
The anatomical neck rings the head.
The **surgical neck** is below. It's a common fracture site.
The **greater tubercle** is lateral. The lesser tubercle is in front.
The **intertubercular groove** runs between them. It's also called the bicipital groove.
The deltoid tuberosity is halfway down the side.
The **capitulum** is a ball on the lateral side. It meets the radius.
The **trochlea** is next to it. It meets the ulna.
The coronoid fossa is a shallow dip in front.
The **olecranon fossa** is a deep dip in back.
The medial and lateral **epicondyles** are bumps on each side.
The radius is lateral, on the thumb side.
The **radial head** is round, like the handle of a bat.
The **radial tuberosity** is a bump below the neck.
The **styloid** process is at the wrist.
**Lister's tubercle** is a bump on the back, a pulley for a thumb tendon.
The ulna is medial, on the pinky side.
The **olecranon** forms the back of the elbow.
The **trochlear notch** wraps around the trochlea.
The **coronoid process** is just below the notch.
The ulna also has a styloid process at the wrist.
The interosseous membrane connects the radius and ulna.
**Supination** turns the palm up or forward.
**Pronation** turns the palm down or back.
Both happen at the elbow, not the shoulder.
So Long To Pinky, Here Comes The Thumb.
The proximal row, thumb to pinky: **scaphoid**, **lunate**, **triquetrum**, **pisiform**.
The distal row, pinky to thumb: **hamate**, capitate, trapezoid, trapezium.
The tunnel of Guyon runs between the pisiform and the hamate. The ulnar nerve passes through.
Five **metacarpals** form the palm. Number 1 is the thumb.
Each hand has 14 **phalanges**. Three per finger, two in the thumb.
The **MCP** joints join metacarpals to phalanges.
The **PIP** and **DIP** joints are in the fingers.
The thumb has one **IP** joint.
